title: Open-source boundary: advisors are the pro differentiator, core schema stays open
summary: The Wheelwright open-source/pro split maps cleanly to the Hub advisor boundary. Framework repo (open) contains WAI-Spoke structure, lug schema (including execute_when and phase fields as inert data), session tracks, hub-spoke sync, teachings pipeline, score_backlog.py, and Ozi monitor. Hub repo (pro/private) contains advisors (Compass, Lathe, Historian, Luci, Distribor), their skills, chain mode, execute-when evaluator, scheduler, and signal triage automation. Without advisors, users get inter-wheel benefits (session continuity, structured memory, teachings). With advisors, the wheel self-sharpens — work creates work, conditions trigger execution, the backlog processes itself.
motivation: Need a clean, atomic boundary between open-source and pro that allows independent evolution of both repos without architectural entanglement.
decision: Hub advisors (and their corresponding skills) are the pro differentiator. Core schema fields (execute_when, phase, blocked_by) are open — they're just metadata. The evaluation runtime that makes them live is pro.
rationale: Advisors are additive intelligence on top of a working system, not woven into the core. This means: (1) Two GitHub repos with independent release cadences. (2) Framework teachings go to all spokes (open). Hub advisor updates go to hub only (pro). (3) The open-source version is genuinely useful — session continuity alone saves significant time. (4) The pro version is genuinely differentiated — autonomous dispatch, fleet management, self-sharpening.
